issues.description: Pre-filter regexes encode a load-bearing soundness invariant that is nowhere stated or tested
issues.detail: Every fast-path skip in this PR rests on the same invariant: 'if the regex does not match, the rule has nothing to report.' That invariant is load-bearing — if violated, rules silently stop reporting real violations. No comment names the contract, no test asserts it, and no spec ties each regex to the set of values its rule would flag. Add a one-line contract comment above each pre-filter ('NECESSARY condition: if this fails, the rule cannot report') and add targeted tests for boundary cases that look skippable but must not be.

issues.description: Performance PR ships with no benchmark numbers or measured before/after
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'Fix *-notation performance' but cites no benchmark, profile, or representative corpus. Some filters (e.g. selector-not-notation's :not( filter) are obviously wins; others (font-weight HAS_NAMED, import-notation url() check) do non-trivial regex work on every decl/at-rule and could be a wash on non-triggering inputs. Attach before/after timings on a representative stylesheet so reviewers can confirm this is the hot path.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE lacks /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it — unjustified asymmetry in keyframe-selector-notation
issues.detail: In keyframe-selector-notation, HAS_KEYWORD is built with the 'i' flag but HAS_PERCENTAGE is not. Today's PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS values are numeric so case does not matter, but the asymmetry is a contract smell — CSS selectors are case-insensitive and the rest of the file assumes that. If PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS ever gains a token with letters, the filter silently changes behavior. Either unify the flags or add a comment explaining why one side doesn't need /i.

issues.description: selectorRegex = /./ sentinel in keyframe-selector-notation is the wrong shape
issues.detail: The 'percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block' branch assigns /./ purely to make walkRules visit every rule. This is a code smell: walkRules still tests the regex against every selector, doing pointless work, and an empty selector would skip versus the unfiltered form. The natural shape is `RegExp | undefined` with a conditional in the walker — the same pattern media-feature-range-notation already uses. Either pass no filter, branch the walkRules call, or unify with the optional-filter pattern used elsewhere in the patch.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED in font-weight-notation may match weight keywords inside non-weight positions of the font shorthand
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED is case-insensitive and uses word boundaries against the full decl.value when prop is 'font'. The font shorthand can contain 'normal' (font-style/variant) or weight-shaped tokens inside font-family identifiers like `font: 12px/1 "Bold Sans"`. The regex conflates lexical presence with semantic position, which the previous full-parse path did not. Add tests confirming that font shorthands with 'normal'/'bold'-shaped tokens in non-weight positions, and values containing var()/calc/custom-property names like --weight-700, behave correctly under both 'numeric' and 'named-where-possible' primaries.

issues.description: import-notation duplicates /url\(/i with inverted polarity across two branches without naming the data
issues.detail: Adjacent lines test the same regex with opposite polarity (`!/url\(/i.test(params)` then `/url\(/i.test(params)`). Correct, but the asymmetric polarity invites a future inversion bug and compiles the literal twice. Extract `const hasUrl = /url\(/i.test(params)` and express the policy with a single comment naming the invariant ('rule reports iff params notation differs from primary').

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation /:/ filter is barely a filter and the perf framing is oversold
issues.detail: Replacing `selector.includes(':')` with `walkRules(/:/, ...)` is roughly behavior-equivalent — postcss still tests the regex against every rule's selector. The only real win is short-circuiting rules with no colon at all, which the prior includes() already covered. Net is neutral; call this a consistency change with the other selector-* rules rather than a throughput fix, and the regex hides the previously-named guard behind a library affordance.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED case-insensitive while HAS_NUMERIC is not — asymmetric flags in font-weight-notation
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED carries /i; HAS_NUMERIC does not. Harmless today because numeric font-weights are pure digits, but the asymmetry will make a future maintainer pause and invites silent bugs if an alphabetic numeric synonym is ever added. A one-line comment ('digits only; no case flag needed') closes the loop.

issues.description: Fast-path filter pattern is duplicated across rules without a shared abstraction
issues.detail: Five rules now use the same shape: build a regex approximating 'might this node need work', test it before the real parse. The pattern duplicates keyword sources of truth (HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, HAS_KEYWORD reconstruct sets that already exist elsewhere), so when the underlying sets change, both must change. Consider a small shared helper like `walkDeclsIf(root, propRegex, valueRegex, fn)` or `buildKeywordRegex(set, flags)` to keep the data primary and reduce drift risk.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation pre-filter regexes are loose and contract is unstated
issues.detail: The 'context' filter /(?:min|max)-/i will match inside identifiers like --max-foo (false positives only cost a slow path so correctness holds), and the 'prefix' filter /[<>]/ assumes < and > only appear as range operators. Range syntax also includes bare `=` (e.g. `@media (width = 100px)`), which the current filter would skip — verify whether bare `=` should be flagged under primary='prefix', and tighten with word boundaries or document the contract.

issues.description: selector-not-notation switches from case-sensitive includes(':not(') to case-insensitive /:not\(/i without note
issues.detail: CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec, so the new behavior is arguably more correct, but it is a behavior change worth calling out in the changeset for downstream users with `:NOT(` in fixtures.

synthesis.summary: Consensus: the PR is a well-shaped performance optimization — cheap pre-filter regexes in front of expensive parser work across six *-notation rules. The pattern is algorithmically sound and the asymptotic work is unchanged. However, every reviewer flagged that the load-bearing soundness invariant ('if the regex does not match, the rule has nothing to report') is nowhere stated, no tests lock the boundary, and a perf-titled PR ships with zero benchmark numbers. Concrete code-level concerns concentrate in keyframe-selector-notation (HAS_PERCENTAGE vs HAS_KEYWORD case-flag asymmetry and the /./ sentinel) and font-weight-notation (HAS_NAMED matching weight-keyword-shaped tokens in non-weight positions of the font shorthand). Recommendation: NEEDS-WORK leaning ACCEPT — add per-guard contract comments, targeted boundary tests, before/after benchmark numbers, and clean up the /./ sentinel and inverted url() duplication.
